texts: bad: "recognizes" is taken as a mental state, so the Council comes out as the experiencer of a perception and the markers as the thing perceived, instead of the Council being the body that does the recognizing and the markers what it recognizes. Use a verb with no perception sense: "The Council acknowledges three calendar markers." Everything else is already right — the three markers as one counted group, the calendar_marker genus, and no tense on the habitual present.
good. the equinox is an ordinary referent starting the season in a plain event, the habitual present correctly carries no tense marker, and each compound keeps only its head genus.

mixed: the content is all captured, but the parse also asserts something the sentence never says — it unpacks "salt-bloom season" a second level down to "a salt-bloom is a kind of bloom" — and "the first" is ranked on a scale the instruction set does not define for a bare ordinal. Writing the season as a capitalized proper name keeps it one unopened symbol and stops the extra unpacking: "The first hard frost starts Salt-Bloom Season." Use that same capitalized form wherever the season is mentioned, so every mention lands on one symbol.

good. the equinox witness closes the season in a plain event and both compounds carry only their head genus — note this sentence did not pick up the spurious "salt-bloom is a bloom" claim that the hard-frost sentence did, so the two mentions of the season are not recorded identically.
